documents.title: Doc 71 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 24 - pit stop incident
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 24 - pit stop incident

details.fact: Car 24 (Van Hoepen) overshot its designated pit-stop position and made contact with the front jack operator, pushing him backwards and causing him to fall.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.4 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations, as applied to the pit lane by Madrid Competition Notes v3 §6.6, for driving in a manner potentially dangerous to another person.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 24. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 65) and heard the Drivers of Car 24 (Van Hoepen) and the team representative. They examined video evidence. At the hearing the driver explained that he pitted during the safety car period and his tyres were cold. He said he entered the pit lane at normal speed and applied the brakes as normal and was surprised that the front wheels immediately locked. He suggested that perhaps the pit lane was more dusty than he expected. The Team Manager explained that he made a very late call for the driver to pit and he too felt that the pit lane may have been unusually dusty in that area. The Stewards considered the penalties set out in the FIA Formula 2 Penalty Guidelines for dangerous driving in the pit lane. Having regard to the exceptional circumstances established at the hearing, including that the driver entered the pit lane at normal speed, applied the brakes in the normal manner, encountered unexpectedly reduced grip and did not deliberately or recklessly approach his pit position, the Stewards considered that the prescribed guideline penalty would be disproportionate in this particular case and imposed a Driving Reprimand.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - failure to follow RD instructions T5 escape road

details.fact: Car 23 (Villagomez) failed to follow RD instructions for the T5 escape road.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code.

documents.title: Doc 56 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - leaving the track and gaining lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - leaving the track and gaining lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 5 (Leon) went off track at Turn 5 and gained lasting advantage over Car 24 (Van Hoepen).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 5 (Leon). This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 50 & 51) and heard the Drivers of Car 5 (Leon) and Car 24 (Van Hoepen) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Car 24 made a pass on Car 5 going into Turn 5. Car 5 left the track, followed the RD instructions and took the correct path around the bollard but rejoined ahead of Car 24 thereby gaining a position off track. After approximately 2.5 laps Car 5 gave back the position. At the hearing the driver of Car 5 explained that while he knew that he was passed on the inside of Turn 5 by Car 24 he was not sure if Car 24 had fully made the corner nor followed the RD instructions and as such was not sure if Car 24 was entitled to the position. He reported that he immediately asked his team to verify if Car 24 had made the corner and if so he would give back the position. The team had to wait for a replay to verify if the driver of Car 24 had in fact stayed on track. As soon as the team reported to him that Car 24 had remained on track he conceded the position. The Stewards also noted that Car 24 confirmed that the position had been fully restored and raised no further issue concerning the manner in which it was conceded. Although the position was ultimately conceded, the Stewards considered that retaining it for approximately 2.5 laps constituted a lasting advantage within the meaning of Article 27.3. The drivers have been trained that whenever they consider that they have gained a position off track they are to give back the position as soon as possible and at the latest within 1 lap. If in doubt it is always better to give up a position than to get a penalty after investigation. In this case the driver of Car 5 was fortunate that the position was still available to be given back after the lengthy delay of 2.5 laps. Given the unique circumstances in this case, and considering that the driver of Car 5 had immediately queried the status of Car 24 specifically if he had remained on track, the Stewards consider this significant mitigating circumstances that warrants a lesser penalty than the standard 10 seconds and gave a Driving Reprimand.

documents.title: Doc 53 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - causing a collision

details.fact: Car 16 (Maini) made contact with Car 22 (Varrone) at Turn 7.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. As Car 16 was not classified, this is converted to a 5 place grid drop for the next race in which the Driver participates. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 5 points.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 46 & 47) and heard the Drivers of Car 16 (Maini) and Car 22 (Varrone) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Car 16 collided with Car 22 at Turn 7. As a consequence of the contact, Car 22 was unable to continue and retired from the race. Car 16 also retired shortly afterwards. The Driver of Car 16 explained that Car 21 had previously left the track and, in his view, had gained an advantage by rejoining ahead of him. He therefore expected Car 21 to give the position back. When Car 21 subsequently moved, the Driver of Car 16 was somewhat surprised by the situation. He then locked his brakes under braking for Turn 7 and collided with Car 22. The Stewards considered the explanation given by the Driver of Car 16, but determined that Car 16 was wholly to blame for the collision. It remained the responsibility of the Driver of Car 16 to maintain control of his car and to avoid contact with Car 22, irrespective of his expectation regarding the actions of Car 21. The Driver of Car 16 acknowledged his responsibility for the incident and apologised to the Driver of Car 22.

documents.title: Doc 41 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - breach of Restricted Period 1
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - breach of Restricted Period 1

details.fact: The Competitor’s operational personnel carried out work on Car 4 during Restricted Period One, outside the permitted working hours and without an applicable approved exception.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 21.6 a of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Car 4 (Herta) is to start the Sprint Race from pit lane.
details.reason: The Stewards received a report from the Technical Delegate (Document 37) that the Team of Car 4 were working on the car after Restricted Period 1 had commenced at 22:30. The Stewards summoned (Document 39) and heard the team representative. The team representative explained that they found a problem with the car just before the start of the restricted period and continued to work on the car as a priority and failed to request the exemption which was available to them had they have asked in advance. They attempted to ask for the exemption after the period had commenced. The procedures for the allowed exceptions are clear and the Stewards find no mitigating factor to vary from the prescribed penalty per Art 21.6. Car 4 is required to start the Sprint Race from the pit lane and follow the procedures prescribed in Article 37.2 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are imposed.

documents.title: Doc 29 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - released in an unsafe condition
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - released in an unsafe condition

details.fact: The Competitor released Car 11 (Montoya) whilst it was in an unsafe condition.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.12 (b) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 1000 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 20) and heard the team representative. They examined the photograph presented by the Technical Delegate, and reviewed video evidence. During the Qualifying session, Car 11 impacted the wall in Turn 11 and sustained damage to the right rear suspension. The driver returned to the pit lane and the mechanics attempted to repair the damage. The lower wish bone was noticed to be severely bent to the point that in one section it was visibly “kinked”. A member of the technical delegate's team took a photograph of the component. The team mechanics for Car 11 made a decision that the car was safe to return to the track and instructed the driver to follow an installation lap protocol with the expectation that they would further evaluate the car upon its return to the pit lane. During this lap the driver reported that “he lost drive” and he returned to the pit lane and retired the car. The Technical Delegate reported to the Stewards that in his opinion the lower wish bone suspension component was damaged to a degree that it was unsafe to release the car to the track. Having heard from both the team representative and the Technical Delegate and having reviewed the photographic evidence. the Stewards concluded that the car was released in an unsafe condition because of the established suspension damage.

documents.title: Doc 27 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - trousers not worn in restricted area
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - trousers not worn in restricted area

details.fact: Trousers not worn in a restricted area (working lane) next to Car 11.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 22.15 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 19) and heard the team representative. They examined video evidence. The team representative explained that the woman wearing shorts was a guest of the team and not an operational team personnel member. The Race Director reminded the following to all the Competitors in Competition Notes in Madrid (art 11.1). Teams are reminded that guests are included in the category as defined in Article 20 of the ISC. Additionally, Article 9.15 of the ISC states that the Competitor is responsible for all acts or omissions on the part of any person to whom the Competitor has allowed access to the reserved area. Furthermore, ‘Article 22.15 of the Sporting Regulations states all team and technical personnel must wear long trousers in the pit lane during all practice sessions and the races. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that a team member of Car 11 near the car was not wearing long trousers during the session and therefore decided to fine the team €500.
